_comment: cannot derive, because the two catalogues genuinely disagree about the name rather
than about punctuation. Each pair was checked against the catalogue record by eye
on 2026-08-24 while grading the Antiochus deck.
'canonical' is the form the adjudicated deck uses; 'variants' are the forms seen in
libraries.csv or in a GUI export of the same manuscript. Add an entry ONLY after
confirming the two names denote one manuscript -- a wrong entry silently merges two

aliases.note: Zero-padded fraction in one catalogue, unpadded in the other.
Halper catalogue number vs Penn/Katz Center shelfmark.
JTS ENA New Series; roman vs arabic numeral for the series.

why_rejected: Accepted during the 2026-08-24 grading session and REVERSED on 2026-08-24
when loading the deck through this table merged two entries carrying
OPPOSITE verdicts: 'Gaster, Moses Collection' is graded NOISE and
'Ms. 1774' is graded WITNESS. A conflict of that shape means one of two
things, and both forbid the alias: either the equation is wrong, or one
of the two gradings is. 'Gaster, Moses Collection' is a COLLECTION-level
string in libraries.csv covering many manuscripts, so it cannot be
equated with a single codex -- the equation is what is wrong.
Kept here rather than deleted so it is not re-derived and re-accepted.
